description: What Excel makes of a formula cell whose cached <v> is empty, or absent, under each type. The package is one Excel saved with manual calculation (calcMode="manual", calcId="191029"), its row 1 patched: A1 <f>1+1</f><v>5</v> is the control (a stale 5 shown means the cache is read, not recomputed), B1 t="b" <f>TRUE</f><v></v>, C1 t="e" <f>1/0</f><v></v>, D1 t="str" <f>"x"</f><v></v>, E1 t="b" <f>TRUE</f> with no <v>, F1 <f>1+1</f><v></v>.
verdict: The control shows 5, so Excel shows the cache. Every empty or absent cached result shows as an empty String Value2 with empty Text, whatever its type: not FALSE under t="b", not an error under t="e", not 0 for a number. Excel draws no line between an empty cached result and none, so the reader reads both as no cached result, except under t="str", where a present <v> is the empty string as it is on a plain cell.
